54292/2025 (amendment of petition) in W.P.(C) 12491/2025
1. Prayer for amendment is allowed without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the respondents.
Let the amended writ petitions be taken on record.
2. The applications stand disposed of.
Heard the counsel for the petitioners.

4. In both these petitions, the challenge is to the Public Notice dated 31st July 2025 issued under Section 21 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013, ('Act of 2013'), with respect to the land described in the prayer clause.

entities.text: Lokesh Lochav & Anr. v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors. WP(C) 11820/2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner claims that, deviating from the scheme as prescribed under the Act of 2013, the Apex Court has fixed a schedule in exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, 1950 ('Constitution'), and the schedule should have been adhered to by the respondents.

9. It is claimed that the Public Notice issued under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 is sans the schedule prescribed and, as such, attracts the consequences under Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 for not completing the acquisition proceedings within schedule.

10. It is the contention of the counsel for petitioners that the schedule, since it is in deviation from the statutory provisions, i.e. Act of 2013 and is fixed in exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, has a mandatory effect and, as a sequel, the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 stands vitiated.
11. Accordingly, since the matter are similarly placed, issue notice.
12. Notice is accepted by Mr. Sanjay Kumar Pathak, counsel appearing on behalf of R-1 to R-4.

Issue notice to remaining respondent, returnable on 22nd September 2025.
14. We make it clear that no further action pursuant to the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 as against the land of the petitioner be undertaken till returnable date.
15. The aforesaid injunction order is passed taking in view the prima facie satisfaction by this Court that the scheduled as ordered by the Apex Court appears to be mandatory in nature.
